newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian court rejects petrol price fix charges.
newsitem.headline: Australian court rejects petrol price fix charges.

text.p: Mobil Oil Australia Ltd said on Thursday that price fixing allegations brought against it and two other refiners and distributors by the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) had been dismissed in the Federal Court.
The company said Justice Heerey found that Mobil, British Petroleum Plc and Shell Australia did not have a case to answer.

A Mobil spokeswoman said the preliminary hearings in the Federal Court, which determine whether there was a case to answer, began in November 1994 and were based on allegations that the three companies entered into a price fixing arrangement in 1991.
Mobil said in a statement that the judge stated that the ACCC "does not have a case, but hopes by the discovery process to fish around in the hope that something will turn up".
"I believe the outcome today confirms what we have always maintained: Mobil does not collude on price," Mobil fuels director Paul Wherry said.
"The petrol market is extremely competitive, and competition in the market is tough," Wherry said.
